Obtains focused histories, performs targeted physical examinations, and reviews relevant records.
Develops an appropriate differential diagnosis and diagnostic plan using sound clinical reasoning.
Creates evidence-based management plans that are individualized to the patient's clinical condition and illness severity; uses shared decision-making when appropriate.
Explains the assessment, diagnosis, treatment plan, return precautions, and follow-up recommendations clearly to patients and caregivers, confirming understanding.
Recognizes when specialty consultation, emergency department referral, or hospital admission is indicated and initiates timely referral with clear communication.
Adapts the evaluation and management for children with chronic medical conditions, medical technology, or special health care needs who present with acute illness.
Identifies and addresses preventive care needs during acute visits when appropriate (e.g., immunizations, health maintenance, anticipatory guidance).
Works collaboratively with faculty, nursing staff, medical assistants, and other members of the health care team to provide efficient, family-centered care.
Provides appropriate supervision, teaching, and feedback to junior residents and medical students while maintaining efficient patient care.

Gathers essential information through a developmentally appropriate history including psychosocial screening (e.g., risk behaviors, substance use, sexual health, mental health, eating concerns, etc.), physical examination, and review of information in the health record.
Uses clinical reasoning to develop a differential diagnosis for common adolescent concerns (e.g., eating disorders, menstrual disorders, STIs, substance use, headaches, sports injuries).
Develops appropriate evidence-based and individualized management plans for common adolescent medical and behavioral conditions using shared decision-making.

Recognizes when referral or multidisciplinary care is needed and collaborates effectively with specialists or community resources (e.g., eating disorder programs, mental health services, substance use treatment programs).
Communicates sensitive topics with adolescents in a respectful and developmentally appropriate manner, building therapeutic relationships. Involves caretakers when appropriate.
Maintains clear, accurate, and timely documentation of clinic encounters.
Demonstrates engagement in learning through preparation for clinic, participation in discussions and literature searches, and completion of assigned presentations or teaching activities.
